items.title: AI Giant Anthropic Confidentially Files For U.S. IPO As Investors Bet Big On AI Future - HuffPost
items.summary: # AI Giant Anthropic Confidentially Files For U.S. IPO As Investors Bet Big On AI Future. AI giant Anthropic said on Monday it has confidentially filed for a U.S. initial public offering, teeing up what could become the watershed moment for Wall Street's AI frenzy. June 1 (Reuters) - AI giant Anthropic said on Monday it has confidentially filed for a U.S. initial public offering, teeing up what could become a watershed moment for Wall Street’s AI frenzy. The crucial step toward a listing comes on the heels of SpaceX’s mega-IPO, which is on course to rewrite the record books as the Elon Musk-led company pursues a $75 billion offering at a $1.75 trillion valuation. OpenAI is also preparing to confidentially file for a U.S. IPO in the coming weeks, a source familiar with the matter told Reuters in late May, adding to a wave of blockbuster listings anticipated in the year ahead.

items.title: SoftBank lines up €75bn data centre investment in France - Total Telecom
items.summary: Posted by Harry Baldock | Jun 1, 2026 | Investment, INFRASTRUCTURE, AI, COMPANY NEWS, Cloud, Data Centres, Europe, News. ###### “France is uniquely positioned to become a leading AI infrastructure hub in Europe,” says SoftBank CEO Masayoshi Son. This week, SoftBank Group has announced plans to invest up to €75 billion to deploy 5 GW of AI-focused data centres in France. “With its industrial capabilities, talent base and national ambition, France is uniquely positioned to become a leading AI infrastructure hub in Europe.”. “SoftBank’s decision to invest massively in AI datacenters in France – a first for the group in Europe – is testament to President Emmanuel Macron’s ambition to position France as a leading destination all along the AI value chain,” said Roland Lescure, Minister of Economy, Finance, & Industrial, Energy, & Digital Sovereignty. France is quickly becoming something of a European champion for AI data centres, with major tech and telco consortium AION pledging to build an ‘AI gigafactory’ in the country just last month.

items.title: Q2 2026 The State of Consumer AI - PitchBook
items.summary: # The State of Consumer AI. ### Series B emerges as the highest-conviction entry point in consumer AI venture. Cumulative consumer unicorn valuations tripled YoY to reach $1.4 trillion by the end of 2025, but the top 10 companies now account for nearly 80% of that total value, making the asset class functionally a bet on a handful of platforms. Meanwhile, a growing cohort of AI-native products have pushed consumer pricing past the $100-per-month threshold, a level that was commercially nonviable before the current wave and signals a blurring of consumer and enterprise-grade willingness to pay. Series B stands out as the highest-conviction entry point, combining a 97.1% success rate with 63.5% annualized returns. Against this backdrop, consumer sentiment has dropped to levels not seen since the global financial crisis, K-shaped wealth divergence is narrowing the addressable middle of the market, and generative AI app downloads have scaled to 3.8 billion annually, underscoring both the depth of adoption and the intensity of competition that private market investors must navigate.

items.title: NYT Publisher Warns AI Companies May Lead to 'Unnecessary Harm' - Variety
items.summary: # New York Times Publisher Warns That AI Companies Are Making Choices That ‘Violate Settled Law’ and Could Cause a ‘Great Deal of Unnecessary Harm’. New York Times publisher A.G. Sulzberger warned that AI companies were making choices that could lead to “a great deal of unnecessary harm” to the news business and the public’s access to reliable sources, in a speech delivered during the World News Media Congress in France on Monday. Companies leading the development of generative-AI systems — including OpenAI, Meta, Anthropic and Google — are “failing to embrace a core responsibility” of their control over the data fueling the technology’s development, Sulzberger said: making sure the public has access to “trustworthy” news. He pinned the cause on the companies’ “hijacking” of the public’s attention, spurred by the content they’ve trained their large language models on, including news articles. I’m warning that AI companies are making choices that violate settled law, threaten the viability of creative work, and appear likely to cause a great deal of unnecessary harm.”.

This will include the development of the Oropesa Tin Project in Andalucía and the project’s alignment with the Robledollano Tin Smelter, in which the company has a binding option to acquire a 50% interest stake. items.title: Strategic development of stable and efficient lead-free perovskite solar cells - Nature
items.summary: # Strategic development of stable and efficient lead-free perovskite solar cells. Lead-free perovskite solar cells have seen rapid growth in recent years and pose a strong contender for future photovoltaic technology due to their non-toxic behavior. However, lead-free perovskite solar cells suffer from stability issues and low efficiency. In 2025, Tin-based perovskite solar cells achieved a maximum device efficiency of 17.13%. In this review, we discussed various strategies to develop stable and efficient lead-free perovskite solar cells. A brief discussion on the lead-free perovskite solar cells as alternatives and their fundamental issue has been presented. Importantly, recent developments in lead-free perovskite solar cells have been presented to emphasize the trends and techniques for highly efficient materials. By altering the A, B, or X site in perovskites, their features, such as bandgap, charge transport, optical absorption, and stability, can be tuned to make them highly attractive for solar energy applications22.").

items.title: Nintech, Mold and Injection Molding Manufacturer, Files for Nasdaq Capital Market IPO - TradingView
items.summary: # Nintech, Mold and Injection Molding Manufacturer, Files for Nasdaq Capital Market IPO. Nintech, a China-based manufacturer of customized molds and injection-molded parts, filed an F-1 to list its Class A ordinary shares on the Nasdaq Capital Market under the symbol NTMJ. The company plans to offer 6,250,000 shares at an estimated price range of $4.00 to $5.00 per share. The company operates from Taizhou, Jiangsu Province, and leverages advanced production equipment and high-precision testing instruments, supported by quality certifications including IATF 16949, ISO 9001, and ISO 14001. Revenue primarily comes from product sales—both injection-molded parts and customized molds—with a small portion from mold repair and processing services. * **Total addressable market**: China’s mold manufacturing sector generated RMB 363.3 billion in main business revenue in 2024. * **Market growth**: Home appliance mold market expected to grow from RMB 45 billion in 2025 to RMB 65 billion in 2030 (≈7.5% CAGR). * **Market position**: China remains a net exporter of molds with total mold exports above USD 8.7 billion in 2024.
